Definition: from G2596 and G1018 (in its original sense); to award the price against, i.e. (figuratively) to defraud (of salvation):--beguile of reward.
BiblicalUsage: Paul warns against anyone who would beguile you of your reward, judging you by visions and humility he does not have.
TheologicalSignificance: I believe a teacher who adds rules to Christ is not protecting me, he is robbing me.
Sources: Strong's Exhaustive Concordance (1890), via OpenScriptures Strong's Dictionary (CC BY-SA)
